overlapEmpty: No dates can be classified under both definitions.
sourceArchiveText: City hourly observations archived by quotsoft / CN-AIR. The PM2.5 daily value is the mean of at least 12 valid hourly values, or the last available rolling 24-hour mean, falling back to the mean of available hours. The daily AQI proxy averages published hourly indices when enough are available, or uses the last available index.
sourceRecentText: Recent station publications and city hourly archives. Station snapshots are aggregated by city. Daily chart AQI is derived from daily mean PM2.5, while the table’s latest AQI averages available published station indices at that time.
sourceCamsText: Copernicus CAMS gridded concentrations served by Open-Meteo. Recent means the short window covered by the latest collection. A daily mean needs at least 18 hours. AQI is estimated from PM2.5 alone.
sourceWeatherText: Open-Meteo supplies recent gridded visibility and humidity. Xi’an also has 2024 NOAA airport visibility observations with humidity derived from temperature and dew point. Coverage varies by source.
sourceEmbassyText: PM2.5 at US Embassy compounds in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shenyang. 2010–2015 is the UCI five-city set; 2016 onward is Department of State AirNow hourly data from an EPA historical snapshot (Beijing/Shanghai/Guangzhou/Shenyang through March 2025, Chengdu through 2020). This site shows 2013 onward. AQI is a single-pollutant HJ 633—2012 estimate from PM2.5, not AirNow US AQI or the official multi-pollutant index.
aqiOfficial: The official daily report calculates an individual index (IAQI) for daily mean PM2.5, PM10, SO₂, NO₂ and CO, and for the daily maximum 8-hour mean of O₃. It interpolates between adjacent concentration breakpoints and takes the largest pollutant index as the AQI.
aqiVersions: HJ 633—2026 replaced HJ 633—2012 on 1 March 2026. For example, the daily PM2.5 concentration at AQI 100 changed from 75 to 60 μg/m³. This site’s recent daily series uses the older PM2.5 breakpoints and rounds the resulting single-pollutant estimate.
aqiScale: Excellent 1–50 · Good 51–100 · Light pollution 101–150 · Moderate 151–200 · Heavy 201–300 · Severe 301–500.
compareMethodsText: Measured columns aggregate monitoring station readings by city. Model columns use the CAMS grid cell at city coordinates. The model column uses up to 24 available hours at the end of its snapshot. Its time may differ from the measurement anchor. Bias averages model minus observed daily PM2.5 over shared valid days. Both above-75 counts use those shared days as their denominator. A dash indicates no overlap.
airportVisibilityNote: Single airport station. Many readings cluster at 9.9 km, near the 10 km threshold. Counts are exploratory.
definition_pm25: Mass concentration of particles with aerodynamic diameter up to 2.5 μm.
definition_pm10: Mass concentration of particles with aerodynamic diameter up to 10 μm.
definition_aqi: An index of air pollution. A PM2.5-only index can differ from an official AQI calculated across pollutants.
definition_visibility_km: Distance at which objects can be distinguished. Fog, precipitation and dust can also reduce visibility.
definition_rh: Water vapour as a percentage of saturation at the same temperature.
definition_coverage: Classifiable days divided by calendar days in the period, through today for the current year.
ruleLogic: Strict inequalities exclude readings exactly on the threshold. AND requires every condition; OR requires at least one. Missing readings produce an unknown result unless a known condition already decides it.

search: Search by city name or pinyin
intro: Haze days across China’s major cities, compared by particulate pollution and local weather.
recentInfo: The default source is the CNEMC hourly archive: national cities from 13 May 2014, Beijing from 6 December 2013. Files come from the quotsoft compilation of the published national network. A day uses the hourly mean when 12 hours exist, otherwise the last 24-hour average. Earlier dates stay missing. CAMS is a model comparison only. The weather definition may still have no data.
staticSiteNote: Static build: charts are baked in at build time. To refresh data locally, run npm run data:update and npm run build:static, then npm run preview:static. No Node API server is required.
compareLead: Latest CNEMC hour for 40 cities, and the CAMS daily-mean bias on overlapping days. Bias is model minus measurement.
compareEmpty: The comparison table has not been generated.
heading: Haze days in {{city}}
mapWaiting: City comparison is a table, not a China map. A national basemap needs an official review number and boundaries that meet public-map rules. This project does not yet have a legally reusable GeoJSON, so the map, map year selector and map export are unimplemented.
ruleInvalid: Enter one to five valid conditions within the allowed metric ranges.

hourlyEmpty: No hourly values for this day.

footer: Dates and daily aggregation use Asia/Shanghai.
attribution: Air-quality observations are from CNEMC public releases, archived by quotsoft / CN-AIR. CAMS model data © Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, via Open-Meteo.
notesIntro: Haze days are counted separately under each definition. A day counts when the selected conditions are met.
modelNotes: Measured data describes a monitoring site. Model data estimates conditions over a grid cell. Station distance, local sources and model resolution can affect comparisons.
thresholdNotes: The PM2.5 and AQI values are analysis thresholds. China’s 75 μg/m³ preset uses the historical GB 3095–2012 limit. The US EPA and WHO presets use their 24-hour values. The weather preset uses visibility below 10 km and relative humidity below 90%.
qualityNotes: Days that cannot be classified are marked as missing. Periods with some valid days and less than {{coverage}} coverage are flagged.
invalidLink: Some link settings were invalid. Defaults were applied.
NO_DATA: The selected range has no data.
embassyCityOnly: US Embassy PM2.5 is only available for Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Shenyang. Change the city or pick another PM source.
